A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NUQLS research, with matching authors, core algorithm, theory, and retained experiments. The complete 24-page v1 and 39-page v2, including appendices and v2's checklist, provide readable material for a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original NUQLS results on toy regression, UCI datasets, image classification, uncertainty evaluation, and hyperparameter sensitivity.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds NTK-convergence experiments, confidence-interval evaluations, further comparator results, and SVHN/ImageNet evaluations.

M1.justification: The core linearized sampler, training objective, Gaussian initialization, and eNUQLS extension are retained. For the new confidence-interval experiments, however, v2 Appendix I.5 adds a 1.5 multiplier to NUQLS variances alongside the existing gamma-tuning procedure, a limited adaptation of uncertainty postprocessing.

E1.justification: v2 adds SVHN classification with CIFAR-10 as OOD data, ImageNet classification with ImageNet-O evaluation, Gaussian synthetic regression for convergence testing, and sinusoidal regression for confidence-interval evaluation. The original UCI, toy-regression, and image-classification coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds PNC to confidence-interval comparisons and evaluates BatchEnsemble, SNGP, and SGLD in classification comparisons. BDE, already evaluated on toy regression in v1, is additionally compared on UCI datasets and FashionMNIST. These are actual comparator additions in Tables 3–4, 8, and 11 and Figure 6.

E3.justification: v2 introduces explicit NTK-variance convergence and confidence-interval coverage/width protocols. Existing settings also change: ResNet9/FashionMNIST NUQLS uses 2 instead of 5 epochs and gamma 0.1 instead of 0.6; ResNet20 uses 100 instead of 50 ensemble members. Table 7 adds a ResNet32 configuration. UCI runtime reporting now includes base-network training while separately retaining post-hoc costs. These are protocol and accounting changes, not same-setting performance comparisons.

E4.justification: New Section 4.1/Figure 2 tests convergence toward NTK-GP variance across training duration, ensemble size, and network configurations. Appendix H.1 compares confidence-interval behavior under extremely wide, partially trained versus finite-width, fully trained networks. Conversely, v1 Appendix C.2/Figure 3's classification sensitivity analysis over gamma, learning rate, and epochs is removed.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 2 reports 95% sample confidence intervals over 10 random realizations, and Appendix I.5 specifies 100 or 50 repetitions for coverage experiments. Conversely, NUQLS's ResNet20 standard deviations disappear between v1 Table 5 and v2 Table 7. The established repeated-run reporting for UCI and LeNet experiments is retained.

E6.justification: v2 adds convergence curves, coverage/width results, BDE regression scores, and additional classification results. ResNet9/FashionMNIST incorrect/OOD VMSP medians change from 0.041/0.119 to 0.182/0.217 alongside changed training settings. ResNet20 NLL changes from 0.236±0.001 to 0.228 with a larger ensemble. Original UCI predictive metrics remain unchanged; larger reported runtimes reflect added base-training costs, such as Energy NUQLS changing from 0.151 seconds to 8.374 seconds total, retaining 0.151 in parentheses.

T1.justification: The main assumptions, convergence theorem, GP derivation, and Appendix A proofs are substantively retained. New Appendix D presents an almost-sure noncollapse argument for parameter samples, while Appendix E derives approximate per-epoch computational costs and ensemble-memory scaling. These supplement rather than replace the central theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract's principal NUQLS, GP-connection, and efficiency claims remain. v2 makes VMSP, already proposed in v1 Section 5.3, an explicit fourth introductory contribution. Remark 1.1 additionally argues that Bayesian methods should prioritize uncertainty estimation over predictive gains, refining the paper's stated contribution and focus.

C2.justification: New Appendix C substantially develops the distinction between epistemic uncertainty and prediction quality, including critiques of NLL, calibration, and OOD-detection metrics. Appendix H.1 interprets NUQLS and PNC as complementary across training/width regimes, and the conclusion adds dependence on adequate training and local linearization as a limitation. The cross-entropy theoretical caveat already existed in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a separate NUQLS package link, pretrained ImageNet-weight provenance, implementation settings for convergence and coverage experiments, and detailed BDE, BatchEnsemble, SNGP, and SGLD configurations. Appendix E adds computational and memory guidance. Existing experimental-code access and much original implementation documentation are retained, while classification tuning guidance is shortened.

R1.justification: Appendix B substantially expands positioning against PNC, SNGP, efficient ensemble methods, and Miani et al. (2024b)'s null-space posterior approach. Additional literature supports the new discussion of epistemic uncertainty and limitations of calibration metrics. BDE's positioning changes from largely explaining its exclusion to discussing broader direct comparisons.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: main-text related work is consolidated into Appendix B, predictive classification evaluation moves to Appendix G, and experiments begin with convergence validation. The introduction is reframed around uncertainty evaluation, classification tuning discussion is shortened, and the appendices are reorganized into dedicated interpretation, cost, and experimental sections.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column to single-column layout. v2 adds convergence Figure 2, four-panel Figure 6, confidence-interval and BDE tables, and expanded comparison/settings tables; removes v1's sensitivity Figure 3; and relocates predictive Table 2 to the appendix. Table 7 also introduces grouped model columns and colored rankings. Several original plots are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation through direct NTK-convergence testing, broader comparator evaluations, and an explicit failure-regime study. Including base-network training costs makes the central efficiency comparison more complete, while expanded implementation details improve reproducibility. Removing the hyperparameter sensitivity study and ResNet20 error bars weakens some reporting, and ImageNet is compared only with a random baseline. Nevertheless, the gains in empirical support, applicability assessment, and cost transparency provide a substantial overall improvement.
